Bill number: HB1498
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1487
 By Powers

 HOUSE BILL 1498

 By Reedy

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 16;
 Title 37 and Title 49, relative to student behavior.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Early Behavioral Intervention

 and Reporting Act."

 (b) As used in this section, "early warning signs" means evidence of safety,

 health, or behavioral issues exhibited by a student and includes, but is not limited to,

 indicators of a student engaging in or being the victim of harassment, intimidation,

 bullying, or cyberbullying; making or receiving threats of violence; and exhibiting signs of

 substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system that teachers and school staff must use to input data of early warning signs

 demonstrated by students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school. Each LEA and

 public charter school shall ensure that each teacher and school staff member is trained

 to identify early warning signs and on how to input data into the computer-based system.

 (d) The computer-based system implemented pursuant to subsection (c) must:

 (1) Align with the harassment, intimidation, bullying, and cyberbullying

 policy adopted by the LEA in accordance with § 49-6-4503; the School Discipline

 Act, compiled in part 41 of this chapter; and with each school safety plan adopted

 by the LEA or public charter school pursuant to the Schools Against Violence in

 Education (SAVE) Act, compiled in part 8 of this chapter;

 (2) Include a database that is capable of receiving and maintaining

 student data entered by teachers and school staff on the early warning signs

 demonstrated by students; and

 (3) Immediately notify the LEA personnel serving on the LEA's threat

 assessment team created pursuant to § 49-6-2701, or the employee of the public

 charter school who is designated to receive such notification, when an early

 warning sign is entered into the system for a student.

 (e) The LEA or public charter school personnel receiving a notification of an

early warning sign of a student pursuant to subdivision (d)(3) shall review the

notification, as well as any other notifications previously received for the student, and

determine whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior.

 (f)

 (1) Each LEA and public charter school shall annually submit a report to

 the department of education that provides the following data collected by the LEA

 or public charter school in the immediately preceding school year:

 (A) The number of early warning signs input into the system;

 (B) The number of early warning signs input into the system,

 disaggregated by the number input by a:

 (i) Teacher, disaggregated further by the grade levels and

 subject areas taught by such teachers; and

 (ii) School staff, disaggregated further by the position,

 assignment, and duties of such school staff;

 (C)

 (i) The number of students for whom more than one (1)

 early warning sign was input into the system; and

 (ii) The number of early warning signs for each student for

 whom more than one (1) early warning sign input into the system;

 (D) A general description of the types of early warning signs input

 into the system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified; and

 (E) A general description of the actions taken by the LEA or

 public charter school in response to each early warning sign input into the

 system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (2) Reports provided pursuant to this subsection (f) must not include any

 details or information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (g) Reports made pursuant to this section must comply with the Family

Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (20 U.S.C. § 1232g); § 10-7-504; the Data

Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, compiled in chapter 1, part 7 of this

title; and all other relevant privacy laws.

 (h) If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or public charter school is

not complying with this section, then the commissioner may withhold state funds, in an

amount determined by the commissioner, from the LEA or public charter school until the

LEA or public charter school is in compliance with this section.

 (i) Subsections (c)-(e) do not apply to an LEA or public charter school that

maintains a system for documenting early warning signs demonstrated by students that

was implemented in the LEA or public charter school before July 1, 2026; provided, that

the LEA or public charter school continuously maintains and utilizes the system.

SECTION 2. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill proposes the "Early Behavioral Intervention and Reporting Act," which would require local education agencies (LEAs) and public charter schools to use a computer-based system to track "early warning signs" in students. Early warning signs include evidence of health, safety, or behavioral issues, such as substance abuse, mental health issues, suicidal ideation, self-harm, threats of violence, or being a victim or perpetrator of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying.

Under this proposal, LEAs and public charter schools must train teachers and staff to identify these signs and enter them into the system. The system must align with existing school safety and discipline policies, maintain a database of the entries, and immediately notify the LEA's threat assessment team or a designated charter school employee. Personnel receiving these notifications must review the data to determine if further action is needed.

LEAs and public charter schools would be required to submit an annual report to the department of education. This report must include the number of warning signs recorded, data on which staff members entered the signs, the number of students with multiple warning signs, and general descriptions of the signs and the actions taken. To protect student privacy, these reports must comply with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and other privacy laws, and must not contain information that could identify specific students.

The commissioner of education may withhold state funds from any LEA or public charter school that fails to comply with these requirements. These rules would not apply to schools that already maintained a system for documenting early warning signs before July 1, 2026, as long as they continue to use it. The act would take effect on July 1, 2026.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: Early warning signs include evidence of health, safety, or behavioral issues, such as substance abuse, mental health issues, suicidal ideation, self-harm, threats of violence, or being a victim or perpetrator of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the definition's scope and nonexclusive examples, including both victims and perpetrators.

assessments.summary_quote: This bill proposes the "Early Behavioral Intervention and Reporting Act," which would require local education agencies (LEAs) and public charter schools to use a computer-based system to track "early warning signs" in students.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the required computer-based system for both entities; the following paragraph explains teacher and staff entry, and the summary separately describes the existing-system exception.

assessments.summary_quote: Under this proposal, LEAs and public charter schools must train teachers and staff to identify these signs and enter them into the system.
assessments.rationale: Conveys both required training subjects and the responsible entities. The existing-system exception is addressed separately.

assessments.summary_quote: The system must align with existing school safety and discipline policies
assessments.rationale: Conveys safety and discipline alignment but does not identify the required harassment, intimidation, bullying, and cyberbullying policy or clearly convey alignment with the School Discipline Act and each SAVE Act safety plan.

assessments.summary_quote: maintain a database of the entries
assessments.rationale: In the context of teacher and staff entry into the system, this conveys a database that receives and retains early-warning-sign data.

assessments.summary_quote: immediately notify the LEA's threat assessment team or a designated charter school employee
assessments.rationale: Conveys immediate notification to the appropriate recipients in the context of entering warning signs into the system.

assessments.summary_quote: Personnel receiving these notifications must review the data to determine if further action is needed.
assessments.rationale: Conveys review and the further-action determination, but omits the requirement to review all previously received notifications for the same student.

assessments.summary_quote: LEAs and public charter schools would be required to submit an annual report to the department of education. This report must include the number of warning signs recorded
assessments.rationale: Conveys the reporting entities, recipient, frequency, and total count, but omits that the data must cover the immediately preceding school year.

assessments.summary_quote: data on which staff members entered the signs
assessments.rationale: Conveys information about who entered signs, but not counts separated by teacher versus staff or the required breakdowns by teaching grade and subject and staff position, assignment, and duties.

assessments.summary_quote: the number of students with multiple warning signs
assessments.rationale: Conveys the number of students with multiple entries but omits the number of entries for each such student.

assessments.summary_quote: general descriptions of the signs and the actions taken. To protect student privacy, these reports must comply with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and other privacy laws, and must not contain information that could identify specific students.
assessments.rationale: Conveys descriptions of signs and responses and the identification prohibition, but does not specify that actions must be described in response to each entered sign.

assessments.summary_quote: must not contain information that could identify specific students
assessments.rationale: Conveys the report-wide prohibition on information allowing student identification.

assessments.summary_quote: these reports must comply with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and other privacy laws
assessments.rationale: Conveys compliance with FERPA and other applicable privacy laws; the omitted statutory names and citations do not change that obligation.

assessments.summary_quote: The commissioner of education may withhold state funds from any LEA or public charter school that fails to comply with these requirements.
assessments.rationale: Conveys discretionary withholding for noncompliance, but omits the commissioner's authority to determine the amount and the limit that withholding lasts until compliance.

assessments.summary_quote: These rules would not apply to schools that already maintained a system for documenting early warning signs before July 1, 2026, as long as they continue to use it.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the prior-system cutoff and continued-use condition, but incorrectly suggests exemption from all rules rather than only subsections (c)-(e). It does not preserve reporting obligations or expressly require continuous maintenance.

assessments.summary_quote: The act would take effect on July 1, 2026.
